title: Exam Technique and Final Review

header.html: Apply the answer method to Standard, Missing word, List and Negative questions; recognize the most common look-alike terms; use the whole-course review sheet

toc.title: The pairs the exam likes to confuse
The lists to know by heart

html:
1The pairs the exam likes to confuse

Pair The difference
Output / outcome / benefit delivered product / result of change / measurable gain
Risk / issue might happen / has happened
Appetite / tolerance (risk) willingness to take risk / limit of acceptable exposure
Tolerance / exception permitted deviation / tolerance forecast to be exceeded
Checkpoint / highlight report team manager to project manager / project manager to board
Project board / project manager accountable, decides / manages day to day
Quality control / assurance checks the product / independently checks the system
PID / project log baseline decided at the start / records updated all the time
Leadership / management inspire people / plan and control work
Project plan / stage plan / exception plan whole project / one stage / replaces a plan when tolerance is exceeded
Starting up / initiating is it worthwhile? (brief) / solid foundations (PID)
Stage boundary / closing end of a stage except the last / end of the project

2The lists to know by heart

List Items
Five integrated elements principles, people, practices, processes, project context
Seven principles continued business justification; learn from experience; define roles, responsibilities and relationships; manage by stages; manage by exception; focus on products; tailor to suit the project
Seven practices business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues, progress
Seven processes starting up, directing, initiating, controlling a stage, managing product delivery, managing a stage boundary, closing a project
Seven aspects of performance benefits, risks, quality, scope, cost, time, sustainability
Three project interests business, user, supplier
Project board Executive, Senior User(s), Senior Supplier(s)
Business case lifecycle develop, verify, maintain, confirm

3Technique for each question style

Style Technique
Standard Read the last line, name the term, eliminate
Missing word Read the sentence with each option; choose the definition
List Mark each statement true or false; pick the pair
Negative Rewrite as "find the false one"; check each option

Old wording alert: themes, six aspects, and the 55% pass mark belong to the older edition. In PRINCE2 7 they are practices, seven aspects and 60%.

Exam tip

. Before you answer, ask: which of the five elements is this about? Then match the term to its element (for example, tolerances belong to progress and plans, roles to organizing).

Exam tip

. With no negative marking, answer every question; flag hard ones and return with the time left.

4Exam Q&A: final review

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which list names the seven PRINCE2 processes?

  • ABusiness case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues, progress
  • BPrinciples, people, practices, processes, project context
  • CStarting up, directing, initiating, controlling a stage, managing product delivery, managing a stage boundary, closing a project
  • DDevelop, verify, maintain, confirm, plan, deliver, close
Show the answer

Answer: C. B is the practices and C the elements.

S2A supplier might be late. Which term fits?

  • AIssue
  • BRisk
  • CException
  • DBaseline
Show the answer

Answer: B. It might happen, so it is a risk.

S3Which statements are CORRECT? (1) The project board is accountable for the project's success. (2) The project manager is accountable for the business case. (3) A checkpoint report goes from the team manager to the project manager. (4) The risk register is part of the PID.

  • A2 and 4
  • B1 and 3
  • C1 and 4
  • D2 and 3
Show the answer

Answer: B. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

S4Identify the missing word. [ ? ] is the permissible deviation from a plan's target before escalation.

  • ATolerance
  • BAppetite
  • CA baseline
  • DA dependency
Show the answer

Answer: A. That is a tolerance.

S5Which principle does a project breach if its board never rechecks the business case?

  • AManage by stages
  • BFocus on products
  • CLearn from experience
  • DEnsure continued business justification
Show the answer

Answer: D. The justification must remain valid.

S6Which report goes from the project manager to the board at regular intervals?

  • ACheckpoint report
  • BLessons report
  • CIssue report
  • DHighlight report
Show the answer

Answer: D. The highlight report is time-driven and goes to the board.

S7Which activity checks products against their criteria?

  • AQuality assurance
  • BQuality planning
  • CRisk analysis
  • DQuality control
Show the answer

Answer: D. Control checks the products.

S8How many marks are needed to pass?

  • A33
  • B40
  • C36
  • D42
Show the answer

Answer: C. The pass mark is 36 of 60.

S9Which process confirms acceptance of the project product?

  • AControlling a stage
  • BClosing a project
  • CStarting up a project
  • DManaging a stage boundary
Show the answer

Answer: B. Closing a project confirms acceptance.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What is the pass mark?

Show the answer

36 of 60 (60 percent).

R2Which learning outcome has the highest weight?

Show the answer

The practices, at 60 percent.

R3Name the seven principles.

Show the answer

Ensure continued business justification; learn from experience; define roles, responsibilities and relationships; manage by stages; manage by exception; focus on products; tailor to suit the project.

R4Name the seven practices.

Show the answer

Business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress.

R5What did PRINCE2 6 call the practices?

Show the answer

Themes.

R6Which aspect of project performance was added in PRINCE2 7?

Show the answer

Sustainability.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Exam 60 questions, 60 minutes, 36 to pass, no negative marking
Weights key concepts 3, principles 8, people 14, practices 60, processes 15
Method keyword, name the term, eliminate, choose the definition
Old wording themes, six aspects, 55% pass mark
Always answer every question
